newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Petroz rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Petroz rated a buy.

text.p: Brisbane-based broker Wilson HTM Ltd recommended oil and gas group Petroz NL as a buy, reflecting recent successful drilling which extended known gas reserves and upgraded possible reserves into the proven category.
"Buy Petroz. The current share price is below our base case valuation of A$1.14 a share and well below our high-side valuation of $1.46 a share," senior resources analyst John Webby said in a report.
The increase in Petroz' value compared to previous estimates was due to the continuing strong oil price and recent successful wells, Bayu-5 and Trulek-1, Webby said.
Webby said the valuation of Petroz was most sensitive to the value placed on the company's share of the Bayu-Undan gas-condensate field in the Timor Sea.
"A more aggressive valuation of this asset suggests Petroz is substantially undervalued and therefore still exposed to a takeover at the current price," he said.

The acquisition in 1996 by Phillips Petroleum of Parker & Parsley's 22.5 percent in ZOCA 91-13 (which contained half the Bayu-Undan field) for A$100 million, underpinned the Bayu-Undan valuation, Webby said.
Recent strong activity in Petroz shares was ahead of a four or five-well drilling programme scheduled for the first half of this year, Webby said.
The activity was also on the back of the recently-completed Trulek-1 well on the southern flank of Bayu-Undan which extended known gas reserves and upgraded possible reserves, he said.
Wilson estimated Petroz' net share of about nine percent in the Bayu-Undan field at about A$110 million.
"Based on the revision in reserves and the recent success with the Trulek well, we believe this value is conservative," Webby said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Petroz reported a 56-metre gross hydrocarbon column in Bayu-5.
At 0340 GMT (2.40 p.m.) on Tuesday, Petroz shares were at A$1.08, steady on Monday's close, and just one cent short of their 12-month high.
